newsitem.title: USA: US farm cooperatives set records again in 1996.
newsitem.headline: US farm cooperatives set records again in 1996.

text.p: U.S. farmer-owned cooperatives enjoyed record net income and business volume for the second consecutive year in 1996, U.S. Agriculture Department said Tuesday.
The nation's 3,884 farmer cooperatives had a combined net income of $2.37 billion in 1996, up from the previous record of $2.33 billion a year earlier.
Business volume surged 13 percent to $106 billion from the 1995 record of $94 billion, led by higher prices for grains, oilseeds and farm supplies, USDA said.
Grain and oilseed sales increased $7.8 billion, or more than 39 percent from 1995. Farm supply sales increased $2.4 billion, or more than 11 percent.

The total value of crops sold by the cooperatives was $79.3 billion, up 13 percent from 1995. Net business volume increased for all commodity groups except rice, which was stable, and cotton, which declined more than 6 percent, USDA said.

Despite the records, the number of farmer-owned cooperatives declined by 122 in 1996. About 40 percent of the decline came from mergers and consolidations, while another 40 percent went out of business. Twenty percent were sold or removed from USDA's list for other reasons.
The slight increase in overall net income disguises more dramatic changes for various types of cooperatives.

Net income for farm supply cooperatives, which primarily obtain fertilizers, crop protectants and other agricultural inputs for their members, increased nearly 17 percent to $942.7 million, USDA said.
But marketing cooperatives, which mainly sell or process crops and livestocks, saw net income decline by 5.6 percent.

Fruit and vegetable cooperative net income dropped 67 percent to $58 million due to lower price for certain vegetables, USDA said. However, sugar cooperative net imcome increased nearly 800 percent to $9.1 million.
